subject: LiveLaunch: Surge causing 5xx/429s — urgent triage & ramp guidance
messages:
From: Amelia Park <amelia.park@fastlane.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-07T09:12:00Z
Subject: Urgent: elevated 5xx/429s during live launch

Hannah —

We just flipped the traffic for our new recommendation feature at 09:00 UTC and immediately started seeing a spike in 5xx/429 responses from Redwood. Error rates hit ~8% over a ten-minute window; several client SDKs started exponential retries and our queue depth ballooned. We rolled back on our side but saw timeouts and retry storms that affected other endpoints.

Attached are a couple of sample logs and a short traffic chart (initial spike). Can you please triage? This launch is customer-facing and we need guidance on what immediate mitigations you recommend (retry backoff changes, temporary rate limits, or routing to a different model variant).

We’re standing by for a call — ops@fastlane.ai is the runbook address.

Thanks,
Amelia Park
Head of Product, FastLane AI

Attachments: fastlane_5xx_sample.log (text), initial-traffic-chart.png (image)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Park <amelia.park@fastlane.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-07T09:27:00Z
Subject: Re: Urgent: elevated 5xx/429s during live launch

Amelia — thanks for the quick heads up and the artifacts. We’re pulling logs on our side now. Two immediate asks while we triage:

1) Can your SDK switch to an exponential backoff with jitter and cap at 3 retries for the next hour? That will stop the retry amplification.
2) If you can throttle client-side ramp (drop QPS by ~30%) we can buy time to fix the backend capacity mismatch.

Connor will run an initial heap/connection check and validate if the failure mode is backend saturation, the rate limiter rejecting requests, or a frontend tokenization OOM pattern. Sean, can you stand up a temporary routing rule to move requests from the hosted pool to the dedicated warm pool for the next 2 hours if we confirm saturation?

I’ll set up a short war-room (15m) at 09:40 UTC.

—Hannah
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: runbook-circuit-breaker-v1.md (text)

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Amelia Park <amelia.park@fastlane.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-07T09:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Urgent: elevated 5xx/429s during live launch

Quick triage notes (initial 09:40 UTC check):

- Symptom: increased 5xx and 429 concentrated on the /v1/generate endpoint for the recommendation model. Error traces show KV-cache misses and rising queue latency on the hosted inference pool.
- Root suspect: model variant in use has larger KV working set and our serving kernels are thrashing memory under the sudden sequence-length distribution from the new feature. This increased CPU/GPU stall time and triggered our internal per-worker queue shedding -> 429s.
- Retry amplification: clients with tight retry loops pushed queue consumption back up after brief recoveries.

Immediate mitigation (recommend):
1) Apply soft circuit-breaker: reject at 60% CPU/queue threshold with 429 + Retry-After header to encourage client backoff. (Sean, I can push the policy.)
2) Route FastLane traffic to the warm dedicated pool (lower concurrency, higher tail capacity) for next 2 hours. This reduces contention and prevents cross-tenant impact.
3) Roll a temporary smaller-context model variant (quantized) for this route — reduces KV working set. (This requires quick config flip; we have a compatible variant available.)

I’ll include sample curl commands and the kernel failure logs in the war-room notes.

Connor
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Amelia — I’m looping in commercial context so we can align on next steps and any request for credits/discounts. We want to move fast to minimize customer impact. Quick checklist:

- We’ll offer a standard incident credit if SLA thresholds were missed during the window; I’ll confirm amount once we have final error-time slices from Connor.
- If FastLane wants us to move to a Dedicated pool for this traffic on an interim basis, I need a heads-up on expected QPS and an agreement to cover short-duration reserved capacity at a reduced pilot rate.
- Can you confirm whether FastLane’s SDKs already include Retry-After honor and jitter? If not, we need them to patch clients (small change).

We appreciate your patience — we’ll send a short executive note summarizing actions and timeline after the triage.

—Marissa
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Park <amelia.park@fastlane.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-07T16:20:00Z
Subject: Re: LiveLaunch: Surge causing 5xx/429s — urgent triage & ramp guidance

Update & actions taken (final at 16:20 UTC):

- Routed FastLane launch traffic to dedicated warm pool instance (dedicated-pool-fastlane-02) at 12:50 UTC. Observed immediate drop in 5xx to <0.3% and tail latency improvement.
- Applied soft circuit-breaker policy (60% queue/CPU threshold) with Retry-After hints at 30s. Policy is logged and reversible.
- Flipped route to quantized smaller-context variant (rec-model-q4_8b) at 13:10 UTC. KV pressure reduced; memory stall metrics improved.
- Recommended customer changes: cap client retries to 3 with jitter and implement exponential backoff honoring Retry-After. FastLane applied a client-side throttle (30% QPS) for the first 20 minutes of their next ramp.

Next steps:
1) Connor to share final sliced error windows + timeline for Marissa to calculate any credits (INF-4821).
2) We’ll schedule a 30-minute postmortem tomorrow to cover a permanent ramp playbook and model-variant suggestions.

Amelia — apologies for the disruption. We have containment and a temporary routing pattern in place if you want us to keep the dedicated pool during your remaining rollout (we can keep it for up to 48 hours with a pilot rate). Please confirm and we’ll lock the capacity.

—Sean
Head of Platform Ops
Redwood Inference
